question.problem:
Find $g(2)$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are two continuous vector-valued functions for which $f(2)=⟨1,1,2⟩$ and 

$$
{lim}_{t\to 2}[f(t)+2g(t)]=⟨-1,7,0⟩\,.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple, and the addition rule for limits, and the fact that both functions are continuous, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}[f(t)+2g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 2}f(t)+{lim}_{t\to 2}2g(t) \\  & ={lim}_{t\to 2}f(t)+2{lim}_{t\to 2}g(t) \\  & =f(2)+2g(2) \\  & ={{⟨1,1,2⟩}_{⏟}}_{f(2)}+2g(2)\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, we are told that

$$
{lim}_{t\to 2}[f(t)+2g(t)]=⟨-1,7,0⟩
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following equation which we can solve for $g(2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}[f(t)+2g(t)] & =⟨-1,7,0⟩ \\ ⟨1,1,2⟩+2g(2) & =⟨-1,7,0⟩ \\ 2g(2) & =⟨-1,7,0⟩-⟨1,1,2⟩ \\ 2g(2) & =⟨-2,6,-2⟩ \\ g(2) & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot ⟨-2,6,-2⟩ \\ g(2) & =⟨-1,3,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$
